subject: Sizing request: private GPU pool throughput & scaling scenarios
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@sierra-cloud.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com
Cc: partners@sierra-cloud.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask: private cluster throughput for 2-phase rollout

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Private on Friday. We’re working toward a two-phase rollout for a regulated tenant: a pilot (Q3) and a production ramp (Q4). Before our architecture sync next week, could you provide an initial sizing and headroom recommendation for a private GPU pool we’d host in our VPC? High level requirements:

- Pilot: sustained 200 qps of short-form generation (avg 40 tokens per response) with <180ms p50 token latency target.
- Production: sustained 1,200 qps with bursts to 3,000 qps for 10–20 minute windows.
- Model: LlamaX-13B quantized variant (~8-bit) with KV cache behavior; mixed request sizes expected.
- Networking: cross-AZ VPC traffic allowed; egress to Redwood control plane restricted during maintenance windows.

We’ll need rough GPU counts, recommended autoscale policy, and any non-obvious networking constraints (egress NAT throttles, NIC oversubscription) that may affect throughput. If you can attach a short scenario spreadsheet, that would be great.

Appreciate it — can loop in infra lead if you want deeper VPC topology.

—Maria
Maria Lopez
Director, Cloud Platform
SierraCloud

Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private cluster throughput for 2-phase rollout

Maria —

Thanks, this is clear and helpful. Quick take while we assemble numbers:

- Pilot: plan for a 6–8 GPU pool (A100/80GB or equivalent) with a small warm pool of 1–2 reserved instances to hit the p50 target at 200 qps assuming batching and lightweight decoding.
- Production steady-state: estimate ~36 GPUs for sustained 1,200 qps given our baseline kernels and 8-bit execution.
- Burst headroom: to absorb 3,000 qps bursts with acceptable tail latency, we recommend burst capacity of ~60 GPUs in the same VPC region plus an admission-control policy to shed gracefully beyond warm pool.

Irene, can you turn these into a quick scenario sheet with assumptions (batch size distribution, avg seq len, kernel perf numbers, NIC bandwidth per GPU)? Karthik — please flag any admission/autoscale ideas you want included.

I’ll send an initial spreadsheet and a runbook draft by Monday. If that timeline is tight for the architecture review, we can meet earlier.

Best,

Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private cluster throughput for 2-phase rollout — scenario math

Jonas —

Attached is a compact scenario workbook (sierra_capacity_scenarios.xlsx) with three tabs: baseline assumptions, pilot calculations, and production burst model. Key assumptions called out in the sheet:

- Model perf: measured 13B 8-bit p50 token throughput = 2,800 tokens/s per A100-80GB when running our optimized kernels and batch=16 for short requests.
- Avg tokens per request (pilot): 40 tokens; production mixes: 40% short (40t), 40% mid (120t), 20% long (400t).
- Effective qps to tokens/sec conversion uses warmed KV cache for 70% of requests, lowering token compute.
- Network: baseline egress per GPU = 420 Mbps under steady decode; bursts increase to 1.6 Gbps per GPU due to larger payloads and KV traffic.

Pilot math (short):
- Required tokens/sec = 200 qps * 40 tokens = 8,000 tokens/s.
- GPUs required = ceil(8,000 / 2,800) = 3 GPUs. Add 2x buffer for warm pool and headroom => 6 GPUs recommended (aligns with Jonas).

Production steady-state (mixed):
- Effective avg tokens/request = 0.4*40 + 0.4*120 + 0.2*400 = 136 tokens.
- Required tokens/sec = 1,200 * 136 = 163,200 tokens/s.
- GPUs required = ceil(163,200 / 2,800) = 59 GPUs.
- But KV cache warm hit assumptions reduce compute by ~30% => 59 * 0.7 ≈ 41 GPUs. Operational buffer and autoscale cushion => we land at ~36 GPUs for steady-state (rounded with placement and NIC limits).

Burst sizing (3k qps for 15 minutes):
- Burst tokens/sec = 3,000 * 136 = 408,000 tokens/s.
- Raw GPU count = ceil(408,000 / 2,800) = 146 GPUs. With KV hits and admission control we target provisioning up to 60–80 GPUs and rely on graceful degradation above that.

Networking notes:
- For ~60 GPUs in a burst configuration, plan for aggregate egress up to 60 * 1.6 Gbps ≈ 96 Gbps. That exceeds single-AZ NIC headroom; recommend multi-AZ flows with cross-AZ link capacity >= 100 Gbps or private NLB with scaled ENIs.
- NAT/concurrency limits commonly throttle control-plane callbacks; recommend dedicated NAT gateways with high throughput or provision with provider private egress IPs.

Action items in sheet: recommended autoscale policies (staged ramp, warm pool retention, fast-shed on tail latency), admission-control thresholds per queue depth, and testing checklist for verifying KV-warm hit rates.

I’m attaching the workbook and a CSV of the admission-control matrices.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Principal SRE, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2029 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private cluster throughput for 2-phase rollout — autoscale notes

Quick notes to add to the runbook: 

- Autoscale backend: prefer staged scale-out (warm pool + predictive spin-up) over pure reactive scale to avoid long cold-start tails on decoder kernels. Use rolling prefetch to populate KV cache in parallel with GPU spin-up.
- Admission control: implement priority buckets (SLA, best-effort) with weighted fair queueing; drop or truncate best-effort at 90% of burst capacity.
- Warm pool sizing: keep ~10% of steady-state GPUs warm for faster recovery; for production that maps to 3–5 GPUs reserved, not shared with other tenants.
- Observability: required metrics: token/sec per GPU, active batch size distribution, kv_warm_hit_ratio, per-GPU NIC bytes/s, and tail latency percentiles per deployment.

I’ll add a short section to the draft runbook (privgpu-runbook-draft.md) with these policies and a suggested test matrix.

—Karthik

Maria —

Thanks for the ask and for giving us the window to run numbers. Summary and recommended mutual action plan below.

Quick summary (rounded):
- Pilot (Q3): 6 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv), small warm pool 1–2 reserved. Test KV-warm strategies during pilot.
- Production steady-state (Q4): target 36 GPUs with 3–5 GPU warm reserve. This keeps p50 token latency in target and provides headroom under our cache assumptions.
- Burst: provision for on-demand scaling to 60–80 GPUs (fast path) and policy-driven shedding above that. Expect network egress planning for ~100 Gbps aggregate if you plan to hit the high side of bursts.

Mutual action plan: 
1) Redwood: send the scenario workbook and runbook draft (attached) — includes admission-control matrices, test checklist, and metric dashboards.
2) SierraCloud: confirm expected VPC link capacity and whether private ENIs or provider NATs will be used for control-plane callbacks. Also share your maintenance/egress blackouts so we can tune control-plane retries.
3) Joint: schedule a 60-minute architecture walkthrough next Tue to validate multi-AZ strategy and map NIC/ENI requirements to provider SKUs.
